correctness.rationale: For all finite connected loopless simple real graphs with adjacency nullity exactly one, disjoint products constrain distinct image columns to the one-dimensional weighted kernel. Kernel support at least three forces disjoint supports. Support two identifies exactly one false-twin pair; orthogonal twin-row column vectors imply one 2×2 block, and equal twin squares plus a neighboring vertex force the block to be scalar identity/swap. Thus every isomorphism is monomial. Its support permutation is a graph automorphism and edge coefficient equations force regularity or bipartite biregularity; explicit diagonal scalings prove sufficiency. The nullity-two star has a nonmonomial continuous leaf-stabilizer. A standalone exact verifier checked all labeled graphs of orders 3–6; the proof does not rely on finite computation.

value.rationale: The graph adjacency versus symmetric random-walk evolution-algebra isomorphism problem is explicitly motivated by an outstanding general singular-graph conjecture. Rank deficiency one is the first complete singular class beyond the established full-rank theorem. The result establishes the precise if-and-only-if degree criterion on an infinite natural class and explains the structural twin-pair obstruction, with a nullity-two example showing the monomial mechanism has a real boundary. This is not a numerical special case or automatic renaming.
